ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: “Not wearing a single thread” names complete nakedness and is extended to a person from whom nothing further can be stripped or removed.
EvidenceBody: Literally, “not hanging a single thread”: not wearing even one strand of clothing. The late Chan records deploy nakedness as a description of a person after successive stripping: Xueguan compares it to taking off clothes and undoing a belt, layer after layer, then asks what could still be removed from “a fellow not wearing a single thread” . Other records pair the phrase with “coming and going freely” or with “the myriad forms all manifest” . The Zen bend is therefore directly visible in its use as an appraisal of a person rather than only a state of undress. The records do not define an inner state behind the image, and this entry does not supply one.
